subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers fail closed on every legacy ownerless session row, or must OpenClaw provide a trusted migration or narrower adoption rule before enforcing this boundary?
rationale: The patch closes a real cross-plugin isolation gap but intentionally removes plugin-runtime patch authority over a persisted row class that predates ownership metadata, so automation cannot choose the security-versus-upgrade policy.

options.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows, document the upgrade-visible restriction, and require deployed proof before merge.

options.title: Require an ownership migration
options.body: Define and test a trusted owner assignment or migration mechanism before denying plugin-runtime access to legacy rows.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows, document the upgrade-visible restriction, and require deployed proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns adjacent session lifecycle and ownership invariants in the same handler, providing the strongest available decision-routing signal.
